title: SELF IMPROVEMENT
mv: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
mvp: “I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.” Philippians 4:13
assignment: List five (5) areas of your life where self-improvement is needed (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: Some people easily give up on their quest or desire to succeed by bowing to resistance or pressure. Self-improvement is the intentional process of enhancing one's knowledge, skills and well-being through self-driven actions. It involves identifying areas where personal growth is needed, such as character, career, or health, and taking purposeful steps to improve them to achieve a more fulfilling life (2 Kings 2:9). This pursuit is often motivated by a desire to become a better version of oneself (Judges 11:2, 8; 2 Kings 2:5, 15).

i: Personal and Character Development: Grow your mindset to think outside and beyond the box and improve on your emotional intelligence, self-awareness, communication skills, etc (2Peter 1:5-7; Ephesians 4:29).
Education: Acquire new knowledge or skill, formally or informally, by reading, taking online courses or attending workshops (Proverbs 15:14; 18:15).

Career and Professional Development: Learn new skills that are job-related and can position you for career advancement, or make a career change that supports your personal goals (Proverbs 12:24; 22:29).
Goal Setting: Learn how to set achievable, specific goals and the action-steps needed to realise your goals (Luke 14:28).
Habit Formation: Build new, positive habits and transform existing ones (Galatians 6:9; Philippians 4:8).
Health and Wellness: Maintain a healthy lifestyle both physically and mentally through practices like exercise, a balanced diet and stress management (1 Timothy 4:8a).

Spiritual: Resist the devil and temptation to sin (1 Corinthians 10:13; James 4:7), equip yourself with God’s word (Hebrews 6:1; 1 Peter 2:1-2) and improve in fruit bearing (John 15:16), and in utilisation of grace and gift (2 Peter 3:18; 1 Corinthians 14:12).

b.x: Self-Improvement often starts with self-awareness i.e. understanding your own strengths, weaknesses and motivations (Galatians 6:3). It is a process that relies on your internal drive or motivation, rather than being pushed by external forces (Philippians 4:13). It requires taking concrete steps to make the desired changes and exploring opportunities that will help you to advance in life (Proverbs 28:19; Philippians 4:8). It involves improving your human relations skills to forge strong and purposeful alliances with destiny helpers (1 Samuel 22:1-2). Diligence and humility are key (Proverbs 22:29; 2 Chronicles 1:10). Self-improvement is a lifelong journey of continuous growth and striving for excellence (1 Corinthians 9:24; Philippians 3:13).
Regardless of your unpleasant experiences of rejection, deprivation or failure, you can still rise to become a significant individual and world changer.
